divergence_floor.measured: real rows of each horizon frame, duplicated and relabelled as generated. The point estimate is zero by construction. The interval is the spread between two copies of the ENTIRE real sample -- score_prediction_horizons scores all real data once and reuses it per window, so the generated window size never enters. It is therefore NOT the floor of the observed comparison, whose binding sample is the generated window. Falsified by measurement: halving the horizon 50->25 should raise a genuine floor by ~sqrt(2); the measured ratio across 17 scores was a median 0.993.

divergence_floor_h25.scale_test: median ratio to horizon 50 = 0.993 across 17 scores; a genuine per-window floor would have moved by ~1.414

scaling_fit.note: Fitted across four horizons (10, 25, 50, 100), not inferred from a single ratio. An iid sampling floor would give beta = -0.5. All three distances are flatter than that and Wasserstein most of all, with R^2 around 0.97-0.99, so the deviation is systematic rather than noise. Dropping horizon 10 -- whose window is shorter than the ~16-message run length -- moves l1 to -0.390 but leaves Wasserstein at -0.223, so within-window correlation at that scale is not the main cause. Consequence: this floor is real and does track the window, but it may not be extrapolated across window sizes by n^-1/2, least of all for Wasserstein -- which is the distance WS-21 reports. An earlier two-point test in this file said l1 matched sqrt(2); four points show that was an artefact of using two.

per_window_null_floor.what: the real stream fed in as the generated input, so each window of real data is compared against the full real set -- the null with the same sample-size structure as the observed comparison
